newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU ministers to meet on satellite communications.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers to meet on satellite communications.

text.p: The European Commission, European Union telecommunications ministers and industry representatives will meet in Paris on Thursday to discuss problems concerning satellite-based communications and the risk of U.S. dominance.
"The discussion will focus on the main industrial, technological and regulatory questions which affect this strategic sector for Europe," the Commission said in a statement.

The conference will seek to "find out whether it's necessary to begin European action in this area," EU Industry Commissioner Martin Bangemann told a news conference, highlighting U.S. activity in the field.
"If we allow anyone to set up a monopoly in this area, then of course we will have done ourselves no favour whatsoever," he said.

Bangemann has repeatedly expressed concern about a decision to award radio frequencies to U.S. satellite communications venture Teledesic, a joint venture whose shareholders include Bill Gates, chairman of Microsoft Corp.
"We do have an anxiety that some players may establish a system which is then the only one for carrying personal communications via satellite," he told the news conference.
EU telecommunications ministers agreed a plan in September for coordinating the regulation of satellite personal communications services.
However, it watered down the role of the EU and gave primary responsibility to the inter-governmental European Conference for Postal and Telecommunications Administrations (CEPT).

The Commission had hoped to set up a single EU system for selecting and authorising the satellite systems that will begin by the end of the decade to offer mobile phone and data communications services.
However, EU member states in earlier discussions resisted the plan because it would have allowed the Commission to draw up criteria for licensing operators and to play a major role in selecting them.
